newsitem.title: CHINA: China, India hope for more military cooperation.
newsitem.headline: China, India hope for more military cooperation.

text.p: Top military officials of China and India, which fought a brief border war in the 1960s, have expressed hope for greater military cooperation, the People's Daily said on Wednesday.

Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian said in a meeting in Beijing on Tuesday with India's Deputy Chief of Army Staff V.P. Malik that improved relations between the two nations would help regional and world peace, the newspaper said.
"We hope that our bilateral military relations will enjoy rapid development at various levels and in all spheres," it quoted Chi as saying.
Malik's visit would boost friendly relations between the armed forces of both countries, said Chi, who is also vice-chairman of the powerful Central Military Commission.
Chinese and Indian armies battled briefly on their Himalayan border in 1962 but tensions have eased in recent years with a series of high-level exchanges and agreements.

Beijing and New Delhi signed a pact in 1993 to ensure "peace and tranquility" along their 4,000 km (2,500 mile) border and last year initialled a treaty to reduce troops and arms in the disputed regions.
